plan: <plan id="math-train/979#0"><block units="1-2"><path units="1-1"><outline>Angela’s compound-interest balance</outline></path><path units="2-2"><outline>Bob’s simple-interest balance</outline></path><conclusion>Angela’s balance is 25657.0837\ldots dollars; Bob’s is 24000 dollars.</conclusion></block></plan>
rationale: Units 1 and 2 compute separate account balances from the common setup; neither uses the other balance.
Unit 2 uses the conjugate root introduced in unit 1 to calculate the product; this is a sequential derivation.
Unit 2 refers to endpoint values first calculated in unit 1, so the two units are dependent.

plan: <plan id="math-train/1336#0"><block units="1-2"><path units="1-1"><outline>Real contribution to the square</outline></path><path units="2-2"><outline>Imaginary contribution to the square</outline></path><conclusion>The real contribution is -7 and the imaginary contribution is 24i.</conclusion></block></plan>
rationale: Units 1 and 2 independently compute real and imaginary terms; unit 3 combines them.

plan: <plan id="math-train/1400#0"><block units="1-2"><path units="1-1"><outline>Contribution from distributing x</outline></path><path units="2-2"><outline>Contribution from distributing -5</outline></path><conclusion>The two inner-product contributions are x^2+8x and -5x-40.</conclusion></block></plan>
rationale: Units 1 and 2 separately distribute different terms of the same factor; unit 3 sums and scales.
Unit 2 uses the intersection equation and its other root from unit 1; the steps are dependent.

plan: <plan id="math-train/1494#0"><block units="1-2"><path units="1-1"><outline>Quadratic and linear coefficients</outline></path><path units="2-2"><outline>Constant coefficient</outline></path><conclusion>The quadratic and linear coefficients are -3 and 9; the constant coefficient is -11.</conclusion></block></plan>

plan: <plan id="math-train/1708#0"><block units="1-2"><path units="1-1"><outline>Restriction from the numerator</outline></path><path units="2-2"><outline>Restriction from the denominator</outline></path><conclusion>The numerator requires x at least 2, while the denominator requires x strictly below 5.</conclusion></block></plan>
rationale: Units 1 and 2 independently derive restrictions from numerator and denominator; unit 3 intersects them.

plan: <plan id="math-train/2246#0"><block units="1-2"><path units="1-1"><outline>Number of adjacent-letter block positions</outline></path><path units="2-2"><outline>Character assignments for a fixed block position</outline></path><conclusion>There are five block positions; for each position, letters have 26^2 choices and digits have 10^4 choices.</conclusion></block></plan>
rationale: Unit 2 counts assignments conditional on any fixed allowed position, without using the five-position count in unit 1; unit 3 multiplies.
Unit 2 identifies face 1 as the only remaining face after the prime outcomes identified in unit 1; that classification depends on the sibling path.

plan: <plan id="math-train/2294#0"><block units="1-2"><path units="1-1"><outline>Orders within the three book groups</outline></path><path units="2-2"><outline>Orders of the three complete groups</outline></path><conclusion>Internal orders contribute 6!, 5!, and 4! choices; complete groups have 3! possible orders.</conclusion></block></plan>
rationale: Unit 1 counts orders within groups and unit 2 counts group orders from the common grouping requirement; unit 2 does not use the factorial values from unit 1.

plan: <plan id="math-train/2486#0"><block units="1-2"><path units="1-1"><outline>Host team and its member choices</outline></path><path units="2-2"><outline>Member choices for the other teams</outline></path><conclusion>The host has four possibilities and 35 member selections; the other teams have 9261 selections.</conclusion></block></plan>
rationale: Unit 1 counts host choices and members; unit 2 independently counts members of the three nonhost teams from the common committee setup.
Unit 2 starts from the position reached after the first two turns described in unit 1; the roll analysis is sequential.

plan: <plan id="math-train/3309#0"><block units="1-2"><path units="1-1"><outline>Base angles of triangle ABC</outline></path><path units="2-2"><outline>Base angles of triangle ADC</outline></path><conclusion>Triangle ABC has 70-degree base angles, while triangle ADC has 20-degree base angles.</conclusion></block></plan>
rationale: Units 1 and 2 calculate angles in separate triangles using their own stated sides and vertex angles; unit 3 subtracts.

plan: <plan id="math-train/3332#0"><block units="1-2"><path units="1-1"><outline>Area accessible directly from the tether vertex</outline></path><path units="2-2"><outline>Area accessible around an adjacent vertex</outline></path><conclusion>The direct sector has area 8\pi/3; each adjacent-vertex sector has area \pi/6.</conclusion></block></plan>
rationale: Unit 1 calculates the direct sector; unit 2 calculates a radius-1 sector after wrapping using the common hexagon and rope setup, without using the direct area.
Unit 2 combines its y-term constant with the x-term constant calculated in unit 1; the paths are dependent.

plan: <plan id="math-train/3456#0"><block units="1-2"><path units="1-1"><outline>Solution set of the lower inequality</outline></path><path units="2-2"><outline>Solution set of the upper inequality</outline></path><conclusion>The lower inequality gives (5/2,3]; the upper inequality gives (-\infty,5/2) and (8/3,\infty).</conclusion></block></plan>

plan: <plan id="math-train/3672#0"><block units="1-2"><path units="1-1"><outline>Restriction from the logarithmic numerator</outline></path><path units="2-2"><outline>Restriction from the square-root denominator</outline></path><conclusion>The logarithm requires x strictly below 3, while the denominator requires x strictly above 1.</conclusion></block></plan>
